text:
Ana K: Heads-up — thinking about moving some per-request policy evals to a cached/subscription model for regional soft preemptive budgets. Could save ~10-20ms p95 on hot paths.
Ryan L: Nice, what does 'cached/subscription' mean here concretely?
Ana K: Instead of running full policy graph for every request, we publish budget allocations and affinity hints every 1s per region/tenant and runtime just looks up the tiny table.
Mike T: That reduces CPU and graph eval, but how do we keep it correct when capacity changes rapidly?
Ana K: Two parts: 1) heartbeat-driven fast-path updates for obvious topology changes, 2) allow stale-but-safe semantics where runtime accepts a slightly stale allocation but has a fallback (hedge to general pool).
Jess P: Stale-but-safe + fallback sounds reasonable. Need to define safety envelope. Eg: if allocation is > actual capacity by X% we must reject or fallback.
Ryan L: Agree. Also we should define probe/goldens so we don't overcommit. If a region reports suddenly lower capacity, runtime should immediately mark allocations as suspect.
Mike T: Ops concern — how do we surface when the runtime is serving from stale allocations? We need telemetry and an alert if fallbacks > 1% of requests.
Ana K: Yep. Proposal: emit allocation_age, allocation_source (publisher|probe|fallback), and a small histogram of decision_path (cached|eval|fallback). Alert if fallback_ratio > threshold for 5m.
policy-sim-bot: Simulation run: 10k reqs across eu-west/us-east with cached allocations every 1s. Fallback ratio: 0.8%. Mean added latency vs full-eval: -12ms. Worst-case regret when region drop: +48ms for ~120ms window.
Jess P: That worst-case window is the risk. Can we shrink it? Maybe use jittered heartbeat (0.25-1s) + immediate push on big capacity delta.
Ana K: Exactly. Also consider per-tenant soft budget vs hard budget: soft budgets are advisory weights used by score routing; hard budgets are enforced caps. Cached model is fine for soft budgets; hard caps still need synchronous checks.
Ryan L: How about API surface? runtime lookup API should be tiny: get_alloc(region, tenant, routing_key) -> {weight:int, expires_at:ts, source:str}. Keep the policy engine as authoritative writer.
Mike T: Love small read API. For safety we need integrity checks on writer side — sign or version the allocation blob so runtime can trust it.
Ana K: We'll include a monotonic version and a checksum. Also runtime will accept only if version >= last_seen; otherwise it requests on-demand re-eval.
Jess P: What about multi-model compatibility? Different models have different cost/latency profiles. The allocation should be dimensioned by model-class or token-profile.
Ana K: Good point. We'll include a dimension 'workload_class' (chat_short, chat_long, embeddings) in the allocation key. That keeps table small but expressive.
Ryan L: Implementation plan: (1) policy engine publishes allocations to controlled topic partitioned by region; (2) runtime subscribes with tiny in-memory cache keyed by tenant+workload_class; (3) fallback to synchronous eval when cache miss or suspected staleness.
Mike T: Dev-ex note: we need tooling to simulate allocation churn so we can validate the worst-case window and tune push thresholds.
Ana K: I'll add a sim job to policy-sim with knobs: heartbeat interval, delta threshold for immediate push, and fallback sensitivity.
policy-sim-bot: New simulation job queued: job_id=sim-2026-03-21-01, params={heartbeat_ms:1000, push_threshold_pct:30, fallback_grace_ms:250}. Results will post here.
Jess P: One more thing — contract for tenants that require strict SLA: reserved/dedicated customers should be able to opt into synchronous hard-eval paths only. No caching for those.
Ryan L: Yes, annotate tenant config with 'strict_allocations':true and runtime will bypass cache.
Ana K: Drafting a short RFC with examples and API: will include example allocation blob.
Ana K: example allocation blob (pseudo):
{
  'tenant': 'acme',
  'region': 'eu-west',
  'workload_class': 'chat_short',
  'version': 42,
  'expires_at': 1746005000,
  'allocations': [{'pool':'hot-gpus','weight':70},{'pool':'shared-cpu','weight':30}]
}
Ryan L: That looks good. Make sure 'weight' is normalized to 100 or include total_weight in blob.
Ana K: Will do.
Mike T: Ops: also add a reconciler that forces full-eval for tenants that flip frequently to prevent oscillation.
Jess P: And add a checklist for the rollout: small cohort in eu-west > monitor fallback_ratio, allocation_age, user-visible latency.
Ana K: I'll add canary steps. Plan: canary 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> global. Metrics gating: fallback_ratio < 1%, p95 latency delta < 15ms, error rate stable.
Ryan L: Sounds good. Any objections?
Mike T: None from infra.
Jess P: LGTM.
Ana K: Thanks — I'll post RFC link once drafted and queue the sim.
policy-sim-bot: Simulation update (sim-2026-03-21-01): fallback_ratio=0.9%, p95_latency_delta=-11ms, max_regret_window=110ms. Logs uploaded to sims bucket :thumbsup:
